Key observations from the test image:
- Single large, elongated/spindle-shaped lesion on a corn leaf
- Tan/gray-brown center with whitish edges
- Lesion straddles the midrib
- Leaf margins show some reddish-brown coloring
- Characteristic "cigar-shaped" form

Top candidates: Northern Leaf Blight (large cigar-shaped lesions), Gray Leaf Spot (rectangular gray lesions), Southern Corn Leaf Blight, Eyespot.

Now viewing one reference per top candidate:

The Northern Leaf Blight reference (Corn_Disease_194) shows multiple elongated, spindle/cigar-shaped tan lesions - very close match to the test image. The test image shows a single large NLB lesion with the characteristic elongated spindle shape, tan-gray center, and lighter margins. Southern Corn Leaf Blight shows a different pattern entirely. Gray Leaf Spot lesions are more rectangular, not spindle-shaped.
